A value that is overwritten or thrown away before anything reads it does nothing. Often it is left over from an edit, or the wrong variable was assigned.

The rule follows every path through the function. An assignment is reported only if no path reads the value.

This rule is on by default.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
function label(user) {
  let name = "guest";
  name = user.name;
  return name;
}
```

{/* bad */}
```js
function finish(job) {
  let status = job.status;
  log(status);
  status = "done";
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
function label(user) {
  let name = "guest";
  if (user) {
    name = user.name;
  }
  return name;
}
```

A variable that an inner function reads is skipped, because that function can run at any time:

{/* good */}
```js
function finish(job) {
  let status = job.status;
  job.onClose(() => log(status));
  status = "done";
}
```

A variable that is never read at all is left to `no-unused-vars`:

{/* good */}
```js
function finish(job) {
  let status = job.status;
  status = "done";
}
```
